heard: A zombie star survived its own supernova explosion. Normally, these powerful runaway blasts completely obliterate a dying white dwarf star. But in the year 1181, astronomers witnessed a strange, rare cosmic blast in the night sky. At the center of its remnant, IRAS 500 plus 6713, a bizarre zombie star survived. X-ray data from the XMM-Newton telescope recently revealed the trick behind the stellar miracle. A carbon-oxygen white dwarf crashed directly into an oxygen-neon white dwarf. This intense collision triggered a partial-type 1ix supernova instead of a total explosion. Today, the surviving star WDJ00-5311 continues screaming through space, blowing an intense stellar wind of carbon-burning ashes. This chaotic remnant proves that a star can actually outlive its own doom.
differences: 'iax' heard as 'one ix' after 'a partial type'
'wd j' heard as 'wdj 0' after 'the surviving star'
